title: Too Much Work, Too Few People
briefing: You now lead a team of four. The quarter's plan has 11 pieces of work and capacity for about 7. Everyone wants theirs done first.
Decide what the team does, what waits, and how you explain it.

context.text: Health and Safety have asked for a follow-up review of yard controls after the Northgate injury.
Procurement has asked for a second look at Kelvarin before the next renewal date.

evidence.title: Requested work this quarter
body: A. Annual risk report refresh (Board, required). B. Cyber assessment of route planning (residual unknown, no fallback). C. Depot expense claim review (Finance request; two duplicate payments found last year). D. KRI dashboard redesign (nice to have). E. Insurance renewal input (renewal in 6 weeks). F. Training slides refresh. G. New depot project risk review (go/no-go in 8 weeks). H. Policy wording tidy-up. I. Supplier risk tiering. J. Second fatigue review. K. Committee minutes archive.
Capacity: about 7 pieces of average size.

evidence.title: Team
evidence.body: Sam (graduate, improving fast), Lina (strong quant), Kofi (experienced, overloaded, two sick days last month), Ines (part-time, compliance background).

questions.prompt: Which items must be in this quarter's plan?

options.label: B. Cyber assessment of route planning (high, unassessed exposure)
G. New depot risk review (go/no-go decision)
F. Training slides refresh
options.feedback: Low risk; can wait a quarter.

questions.prompt: Finance's expense review (C) doesn't make the cut. What do you do with it?

options.label: Ask Finance to run an automated duplicate-payment check now; schedule the full review next quarter
options.feedback: A cheap interim control covers the known failure while the full review waits, and the trade-off is on record.

options.label: Drop it this quarter: last year's duplicates were small and Finance can recover any it finds
options.feedback: Duplicates are a symptom; no review means nobody looks for deliberate abuse.

schedules.description: A depot manager is found to have claimed the same fuel receipts at two depots for a year

options.label: Squeeze it in by adding it to Kofi's list, since he knows the expenses process
options.feedback: Kofi is already overloaded; stretching him risks every item he holds.

questions.prompt: How do you allocate the cyber assessment (B), the hardest piece?

options.label: Lina leads with Sam paired to learn and your review at midpoint; Kofi hands two items to Ines
options.feedback: Matches strength to the hardest work, develops Sam, and protects Kofi.

options.label: Kofi: he is the most experienced, and the cyber assessment is the highest-stakes piece of work
options.feedback: Experience matters, but loading him further after two sick days risks burnout and delay.

options.label: Take it yourself: as team lead you should own the hardest and most visible work
options.feedback: Leaders who take the hardest work stop leading the team.

questions.prompt: How do you tell the requesters whose work waits?

options.label: Publish the plan and ranking criteria, tell each requester personally, and offer interim help
options.feedback: Clear criteria make 'not now' fair and predictable.

options.label: Let the published plan speak for itself and handle questions individually as requesters notice
options.feedback: Stakeholders discover it late and lose trust in the team.

options.label: Accept all eleven items and ask the team to work extra hours for the quarter
options.feedback: Overpromising delivers late, low-quality work and burns out the team.

questions.prompt: Where should the decision about deferred work be recorded?

options.label: In the Risk Committee pack as the agreed work plan, with deferred items and their interim controls
options.feedback: The committee owns the risk appetite for not doing work.

options.label: In the team's planning tracker, where every requester can see the status and date of their item
options.feedback: Decisions to accept risk should be visible to the body that owns appetite.

options.label: Nowhere formal: deferring work is a normal management decision, not a risk decision

lesson: Prioritise risk work by exposure, deadline and mandate; put the hardest work where the strength is; and make deferrals visible, with interim controls.
